links.note: What feeling both pads express towards the prabhu -- deep bhakti and prem, which is the pads' stated main subject under 32341. 32346 loses: pad 2's anticipation is only half the answer, and the question asks for the bhaav shared by both.

How pad 1 describes Nandlal's beauty -- the model answer keys entirely on ornaments and names the vaijayanti maala, and 32343 is where Meera identifies him by his pahnaava and saaj. 32342 loses: not one of its words -- mohini moorat, saanvari soorat, vishaal naina -- appears in this answer.
Sawan's effect on her mind in pad 2 -- umang plus the aabhaas of the Lord's arrival, 32346's umagyo-and-bhanak pair. 32345 loses: it names the month and calls it pleasing, not the sensed arrival.
Why she calls him 'bhakt vachhal Gopal' -- pad 1's chhaap line, carried by 32344. 32341 loses: the opening vinti is her request and says nothing about shielding devotees.
Meaning of 'kshudra ghantika katitat sobhit, noopur shabd rasaal' -- 32344's own line, waist bells and anklets. 32343 loses: its saaj is the murli and the maala, above the waist.

Describe Sawan's beauty on the strength of 'barse badariya Sawan ki' -- the stem quotes 32345's opening line and asks the lesson's own season question, which 32345's description names. 32346 loses: it gives the reason the season pleases her, not the description of the season.

Krishna's roop-saundarya AND shringaar -- the answer's weight is the saaj (murli, vaijayanti maala, karadhani, noopur), and 32343 is the concept whose description makes the pahnaava and saaj his identifying mark. 32342 loses: it covers only the opening face clause of a five-clause answer.

Features of Meera's bhakti-bhaav -- sagun bhakti, aatmasamarpan, Krishna as beloved and aaraadhya: the pads' subject of prem and bhakti that 32341 holds. 32344 loses: 'bhakt vachhal' describes the Lord's disposition, not the devotee's.

Detailed beauty of Nandlal, physical features asked for first -- the answer opens on the moorti, the saanvla rang and the vishaal netra, 32342's triad, and only then lists ornaments. 32343 loses: its murli and maala come after the shaareerik vishesh'taayen the question leads with.

Pad 2's chitran of the month of Sawan and her manobhaav -- 32345 is where the season is named together with its effect on the mind ('Sawan ki man bhaavan ki'), the exact pairing asked for. 32346 loses: it is the single causal line, while this asks for the whole depiction of month plus mood.

Comparing the Lord's svaroop and her prem and samarpan across both pads -- the devotion-subject concept. 32342 loses: pad 1's face description is one side of the comparison only, and pad 2 has no face in it.

Evaluating the pads as bhakti-kaavya, with bhaasha, ras and alankaar -- the answer turns on her bhakti-kaavya's simplicity and the blend of shringaar with bhakti ras, i.e. 32341's prem-and-bhakti subject. 32347 loses: it owns the sound exercise, but only for pad 2's rain words, not the lesson's language and ras as a whole.

Central bhaav of both pads, then Meera's life and the bhakti tradition -- the central bhaav is ananya bhakti and prem for Krishna, 32341's subject. 32345 and 32346 lose: they are pad 2's season and its cause, and the question spans both pads; the biography half has no concept of its own in this set.

How her prem and samarpan to her aaraadhyadev is expressed across both poems -- the pads' devotion subject. 32344 loses: its chhaap states the Lord's grace towards devotees, the mirror of what this asks about the devotee.

The samanvay of nature and feeling -- 32346 is where the link is actually made: the rain is dear not in itself but because it brings news of the meeting. 32345 loses: it names the season and the gladness without joining them causally.

Which form of bhakti and prem the pads show -- maadhurya/daampatya bhaav, i.e. the prem-and-bhakti subject 32341 carries. 32342 loses: the saanvari soorat she adores is the object of that bhaav, not its form.

Long stem, sub-question at the end: which month's rain is described -- Shraavan, from 32345's opening line, and all four options are months. 32346 loses: the bhanak is not what this sub-question tests.

Sub-question: when she gets the bhanak of Krishna's coming -- the bhanak is 32346's own line. 32345 loses: its badariya is only the trigger named in the option text, while the tested phrase is the bhanak.
Sub-question: meaning of 'daamin dam kai' -- lightning flashing in the sky, 32347's line. 32348 loses: 'thandi thandi hava ka chalna', its content, is one of the wrong options here.
Sub-question: WHY Sawan pleases her -- because the badli makes her sense Krishna's coming, 32346's reason-giving line. 32345 loses: it states that Sawan is man-bhaavan; the why is the bhanak.

Sub-question: what happens when clouds close in from all four sides -- lightning flashes and the rain sets in, both halves of 32347's line. 32348 loses: its drizzle and breeze come after, and are not what the gathering clouds produce here.
Sub-question: where Meera asks Krishna to dwell -- in her nayan, 32341's opening vinti, with hriday and man as distractors. 32342 loses: it is the form's description, not the place she asks for.
Sub-question: what Krishna's eyes are like -- bade, from 'naina bane vishaal', 32342's line. 32341 loses: the eyes in it are Meera's own, the dwelling she offers.

Sub-question: what sound his ghunghroo make -- sureeli, from 'kshudra ghantika ... noopur shabd rasaal', 32344's line, with 'kshudra' itself planted as a distractor. 32343 loses: the sound it holds is the murli's at the lips.
Sub-question: whom she calls Nandlal and why -- Krishna as Nand's lal, the vocative the opening vinti addresses. 32344 loses: its chhaap calls him Gopal, a different name in a different line.
Sub-question: what she pleads through 'baso mere nainan mein Nandlal' -- 32341's line itself, the nivedan to dwell in her eyes. 32342 loses: it is what she sees once he is there.

Sub-question: which element of beauty 'kshudra ghantika katitat sobhit' brings out -- the entry of sweet sound into his beauty, which is 32344's line and its rasaal ring. 32343 loses: the murli is sound too, but the stem quotes the waist-bell line.
Sub-question: which quality 'bhakt vachhal Gopal' underlines -- karuna and prem for his devotees, pad 1's chhaap under 32344. 32341 loses: the vinti is her request, not his quality.

Sub-question: what Nandlal's svaroop IS for Meera -- a dear, intimate form full of beauty and bhakti, i.e. the pad's prem-and-bhakti subject. 32342 loses: it answers what he looks like, while every option here is about what he is to her.

Sub-question: where she wants to house Nandlal and why -- in her nainan, 32341's vinti, which the question leads with. 32342 loses: it supplies only the reason clause (the mohini moorat she is charmed by), not the 'where'.

Sub-question: which ornaments and objects are described -- the list opens with the murli at the lips and the vaijayanti maala at the heart, and 32343 is where the saaj becomes his identifying mark. 32344 loses: the ghantika and noopur are the tail of the same list.

Sub-question: which ritu is described, the one that pleases her mind -- varsha; this is the lesson's season question plus the 'man bhaavan' tag, both of which 32345 holds. 32346 loses: it is why the season pleases her, not the naming of it.
Sub-question: why her mind filled with umang -- on hearing Hari's aahat, 32346's own line. 32347 loses: its thunder and rain-spray are precisely the wrong options offered here.
Sub-question: what 'daamin dam kai jhar laavan ki' conveys -- the flash of lightning and the sheet of rain, 32347's line. 32348 loses: 'sheetal pavan', its content, is a wrong option here.

Sub-question: which changes in nature Meera notes -- the answer leads with clouds gathering from all four sides, lightning and the jhadi, 32347's line. 32348 loses: the tiny drops and cool breeze are the answer's closing clause, not its subject.
Sub-question: what she experiences on hearing the 'bhanak' -- the mind fills with umang, 32346's umagyo, named in the stem by that very word. 32345 loses: bhanak does not occur in it at all.
Sub-question: what comes umad-ghumad from 'chahun dish' -- the clouds, 32347's line. 32348 loses: 'thandi hava' is a distractor drawn from its line.
Sub-question: what 'daamin' symbolises -- the flash of lightning, 32347's own image. 32348 loses: its sheetal pavan is one of the wrong options.
Sub-question: what Giridhar Nagar sings -- aanand and mangal songs, pad 2's chhaap line under 32348. 32344 loses: pad 1's chhaap has no singing in it.

Sub-question: how the rain's vaataavaran is described -- in the quoted lines the atmosphere is set by the nanhin-nanhin drops and the sheetal, sohaavan breeze, where the picture settles, and 32348 owns that close. 32347 loses: the clouds and lightning are the event, already tested by the three other items on this same quoted block.

Sub-question: explain the bhaav of 'sheetal pavan sohaavan ki' -- 32348's description names this exact line as the one the lesson's line-discussion exercise asks about. 32347 loses: its line ends at 'jhar laavan ki'.
